title: MamTra: A Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Backbone for Speech Synthesis
summary: Despite the remarkable quality of LLM-based text-to-speech systems, their reliance on autoregressive Transformers leads to quadratic computational complexity, which severely limits practical applications. Linear-time alternatives, notably Mamba, offer a potential remedy; however, they often sacrifice the global context essential for expressive synthesis. In this paper, we propose MamTra, an interleaved Mamba-Transformer framework designed to leverage the advantages of Mamba's efficiency and Transformers' modeling capability. We also introduce novel knowledge transfer strategies to distill insights from a pretrained Transformer into our hybrid architecture, thereby bypassing the prohibitive costs of training from scratch. Systematic experiments identify the optimal hybrid configuration, and demonstrate that MamTra reduces inference VRAM usage by up to 34% without compromising speech fidelity - even trained on only 2% of the original training dataset. Audio samples are available at https://mamtratts.github.io.

AI.tldr: MamTra: A hybrid Mamba-Transformer framework for efficient text-to-speech synthesis that reduces VRAM usage by 34% while maintaining speech quality, trained on only 2% of original data.
AI.motivation: Current LLM-based TTS systems suffer from quadratic computational complexity due to autoregressive Transformers, limiting practical applications. Linear-time alternatives like Mamba sacrifice global context needed for expressive synthesis.
AI.method: Proposed MamTra: an interleaved Mamba-Transformer framework combining Mamba's efficiency with Transformers' modeling capability. Introduced novel knowledge transfer strategies to distill insights from pretrained Transformers into the hybrid architecture, avoiding expensive training from scratch.
AI.result: Systematic experiments identified optimal hybrid configuration. MamTra reduces inference VRAM usage by up to 34% without compromising speech fidelity, even when trained on only 2% of the original training dataset.
AI.conclusion: MamTra successfully addresses the efficiency limitations of Transformer-based TTS while preserving expressive synthesis quality through a hybrid architecture and knowledge transfer techniques.

title: Self-Supervised Speech Models Encode Phonetic Context via Position-dependent Orthogonal Subspaces
summary: Transformer-based self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) are often described as contextualized, yet what this entails remains unclear. Here, we focus on how a single frame-level S3M representation can encode phones and their surrounding context. Prior work has shown that S3Ms represent phones compositionally; for example, phonological vectors such as voicing, bilabiality, and nasality vectors are superposed in the S3M representation of [m]. We extend this view by proposing that phonological information from a sequence of neighboring phones is also compositionally encoded in a single frame, such that vectors corresponding to previous, current, and next phones are superposed within a single frame-level representation. We show that this structure has several properties, including orthogonality between relative positions, and emergence of implicit phonetic boundaries. Together, our findings advance our understanding of context-dependent S3M representations.

AI.tldr: S3Ms compositionally encode not just current phone features but also neighboring phones' phonological information in single frame representations, with orthogonal position encoding and implicit phonetic boundaries.
AI.motivation: To clarify what "contextualized" means in transformer-based self-supervised speech models (S3Ms), specifically investigating how single frame-level representations encode phones and their surrounding context.
AI.method: Extend compositional view of S3M representations by proposing that phonological information from neighboring phones is compositionally encoded in single frames, with vectors for previous, current, and next phones superposed within frame-level representations.
AI.result: Demonstrate this structure has several properties: orthogonality between relative positions, emergence of implicit phonetic boundaries, and compositional encoding of neighboring phone information in single frames.
AI.conclusion: Findings advance understanding of context-dependent S3M representations by showing they compositionally encode both current phone features and contextual information from neighboring phones in single frame representations.

title: Bounds on Agreement between Subjective and Objective Measurements
comment: Currently under review at IEEE Transactions on Multimedia. Submitted 5 November 2025, revised 3 March 2026
summary:
Objective estimators of multimedia quality are often judged by comparing estimates with subjective "truth data," most often via Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) or mean-squared error (MSE). But subjective test results contain noise, so striving for a PCC of 1.0 or an MSE of 0.0 is neither realistic nor repeatable. Numerous efforts have been made to acknowledge and appropriately accommodate subjective test noise in objective-subjective comparisons, typically resulting in new analysis frameworks and figures-of-merit. We take a different approach. By making only basic assumptions, we derive bounds on PCC and MSE that can be expected for a subjective test.
  Consistent with intuition, these bounds are functions of subjective vote variance. When a subjective test includes vote variance information, the calculation of the bounds is easy, and in this case we say the resulting bounds are "fully data-driven." We provide two options for calculating bounds in cases where vote variance information is not available. One option is to use vote variance information from other subjective tests that do provide such information, and the second option is to use a model for subjective votes.
  Thus we introduce a binomial-based model for subjective votes (BinoVotes) that naturally leads to a mean opinion score (MOS) model, named BinoMOS, with multiple unique desirable properties. BinoMOS reproduces the discrete nature of MOS values and its dependence on the number of votes per file. This modeling provides vote variance information required by the PCC and MSE bounds and we compare this modeling with data from 18 subjective tests. The modeling yields PCC and MSE bounds that agree very well with those found from the data directly. These results allow one to set expectations for the PCC and MSE that might be achieved for any subjective test, even those where vote variance information is not available.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces statistical bounds for Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) and mean-squared error (MSE) in objective-subjective quality assessment, accounting for subjective test noise, and proposes a binomial-based model (BinoVotes/BinoMOS) to estimate vote variance when not directly available.
AI.motivation: Traditional objective quality estimators are evaluated against subjective "truth data" using PCC or MSE, but subjective tests contain inherent noise, making perfect correlation (PCC=1.0 or MSE=0.0) unrealistic. Existing approaches create new analysis frameworks; this work instead derives fundamental bounds on achievable PCC/MSE given subjective test noise.
AI.method: Derives theoretical bounds on PCC and MSE as functions of subjective vote variance. When variance data is unavailable, provides two approaches: 1) using variance from other tests, or 2) using a novel binomial-based subjective vote model (BinoVotes) that leads to a mean opinion score model (BinoMOS) capturing discrete MOS nature and vote count dependence.
AI.result: The BinoMOS model reproduces discrete MOS characteristics and provides vote variance estimates. Validation against 18 subjective tests shows the modeling yields PCC and MSE bounds that closely match those calculated directly from data, enabling realistic performance expectations even without direct variance information.
AI.conclusion: The derived bounds provide realistic expectations for objective estimator performance given subjective test noise. The BinoVotes/BinoMOS modeling approach successfully estimates required variance information, making the bounds applicable even to tests lacking variance data, thereby improving evaluation methodology for multimedia quality assessment.

title: Optimizing Task Completion Time Updates Using POMDPs
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, submitted to American Control Conference 2026
summary: Managing announced task completion times is a fundamental control problem in project management. While extensive research exists on estimating task durations and task scheduling, the problem of when and how to update completion times communicated to stakeholders remains understudied. Organizations must balance announcement accuracy against the costs of frequent timeline updates, which can erode stakeholder trust and trigger costly replanning. Despite the prevalence of this problem, current approaches rely on static predictions or ad-hoc policies that fail to account for the sequential nature of announcement management. In this paper, we formulate the task announcement problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) where the control policy must decide when to update announced completion times based on noisy observations of true task completion. Since most state variables (current time and previous announcements) are fully observable, we leverage the Mixed Observability MDP (MOMDP) framework to enable more efficient policy optimization. Our reward structure captures the dual costs of announcement errors and update frequency, enabling synthesis of optimal announcement control policies. Using off-the-shelf solvers, we generate policies that act as feedback controllers, adaptively managing announcements based on belief state evolution. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in both accuracy and announcement stability compared to baseline strategies, achieving up to 75\% reduction in unnecessary updates while maintaining or improving prediction accuracy.

AI.tldr: The paper formulates task announcement management as a POMDP/MOMDP problem to optimize when to update completion times, balancing accuracy against update costs.
AI.motivation: Organizations need to balance announcement accuracy with the costs of frequent timeline updates, which can erode stakeholder trust and trigger replanning. Current approaches rely on static predictions or ad-hoc policies that don't account for the sequential nature of announcement management.
AI.method: Formulates the task announcement problem as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), specifically using the Mixed Observability MDP (MOMDP) framework since most state variables are fully observable. Uses off-the-shelf solvers to generate policies that act as feedback controllers based on belief state evolution.
AI.result: Simulation results show significant improvements in both accuracy and announcement stability compared to baseline strategies, achieving up to 75% reduction in unnecessary updates while maintaining or improving prediction accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The POMDP/MOMDP framework provides an effective approach for optimal announcement control policies that balance accuracy and update frequency, outperforming traditional static or ad-hoc approaches.

title: Mask2Flow-TSE: Two-Stage Target Speaker Extraction with Masking and Flow Matching
summary: Target speaker extraction (TSE) extracts the target speaker's voice from overlapping speech mixtures given a reference utterance. Existing approaches typically fall into two categories: discriminative and generative. Discriminative methods apply time-frequency masking for fast inference but often over-suppress the target signal, while generative methods synthesize high-quality speech at the cost of numerous iterative steps. We propose Mask2Flow-TSE, a two-stage framework combining the strengths of both paradigms. The first stage applies discriminative masking for coarse separation, and the second stage employs flow matching to refine the output toward target speech. Unlike generative approaches that synthesize speech from Gaussian noise, our method starts from the masked spectrogram, enabling high-quality reconstruction in a single inference step. Experiments show that Mask2Flow-TSE achieves comparable performance to existing generative TSE methods with approximately 85M parameters.

AI.tldr: Mask2Flow-TSE is a two-stage target speaker extraction framework combining discriminative masking for coarse separation with flow matching refinement for high-quality speech in single inference step.
AI.motivation: Existing TSE approaches have trade-offs: discriminative methods using time-frequency masking are fast but often over-suppress target signals, while generative methods produce high-quality speech but require numerous iterative steps. There's a need to combine the strengths of both paradigms.
AI.method: Two-stage framework: 1) First stage applies discriminative masking for coarse separation, 2) Second stage employs flow matching to refine the output toward target speech. Unlike generative approaches that start from Gaussian noise, Mask2Flow-TSE starts from the masked spectrogram, enabling high-quality reconstruction in a single inference step.
AI.result: Mask2Flow-TSE achieves comparable performance to existing generative TSE methods with approximately 85M parameters, demonstrating effective combination of discriminative and generative approaches.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Mask2Flow-TSE framework successfully bridges discriminative and generative paradigms for target speaker extraction, offering high-quality speech reconstruction with single-step inference while maintaining competitive performance with existing methods.

title: Ising-ReRAM: A Low Power Ising Machine ReRAM Crossbar for NP Problems
comment: 4 pages + 1 page reference, 4 figures, 2 tables, targeting IEEE conference (e.g. ISCAS)
summary: Computational workloads are growing exponentially, driving power consumption to unsustainable levels. Efficiently distributing large-scale networks is an NP-Complete problem equivalent to Boolean satisfiability (SAT), making it one of the core challenges in modern computation. To address this, physics and device inspired methods such as Ising systems have been explored for solving SAT more efficiently. In this work, we implement an Ising model equivalence of the 3-SAT problem using a ReRAM crossbar fabricated in the Skywater 130 nm CMOS process. Our ReRAM-based algorithm achieves $91.0\%$ accuracy in matrix representation across iterative reprogramming cycles. Additionally, we establish a foundational energy profile by measuring the energy costs of small sub-matrix structures within the problem space, demonstrating under linear growth trajectory for combining sub-matrices into larger problems. These results demonstrate a promising platform for developing scalable architectures to accelerate NP-Complete problem solving.

AI.tldr: ReRAM crossbar implementation of Ising model for 3-SAT achieves 91% accuracy with linear energy scaling for NP-complete problem solving.
AI.motivation: Exponential growth in computational workloads and power consumption requires more efficient solutions for NP-Complete problems like SAT, which are fundamental challenges in modern computation.
AI.method: Implemented Ising model equivalence of 3-SAT problem using ReRAM crossbar fabricated in Skywater 130 nm CMOS process, with iterative reprogramming cycles and energy measurement of sub-matrix structures.
AI.result: Achieved 91.0% accuracy in matrix representation across iterative reprogramming cycles, established foundational energy profile showing linear growth trajectory for combining sub-matrices into larger problems.
AI.conclusion: ReRAM-based approach demonstrates promising platform for developing scalable architectures to accelerate NP-Complete problem solving with efficient energy scaling.

title: DAST: A Dual-Stream Voice Anonymization Attacker with Staged Training
summary: Voice anonymization masks vocal traits while preserving linguistic content, which may still leak speaker-specific patterns. To assess and strengthen privacy evaluation, we propose a dual-stream attacker that fuses spectral and self-supervised learning features via parallel encoders with a three-stage training strategy. Stage I establishes foundational speaker-discriminative representations. Stage II leverages the shared identity-transformation characteristics of voice conversion and anonymization, exposing the model to diverse converted speech to build cross-system robustness. Stage III provides lightweight adaptation to target anonymized data. Results on the VoicePrivacy Attacker Challenge (VPAC) dataset demonstrate that Stage II is the primary driver of generalization, enabling strong attacking performance on unseen anonymization datasets. With Stage III, fine-tuning on only 10\% of the target anonymization dataset surpasses current state-of-the-art attackers in terms of EER.

AI.tldr: Dual-stream attacker with three-stage training improves voice anonymization privacy evaluation by fusing spectral and self-supervised features, achieving state-of-the-art performance on VPAC dataset.
AI.motivation: Voice anonymization may still leak speaker-specific patterns despite masking vocal traits, requiring stronger privacy evaluation methods to assess and improve anonymization robustness.
AI.method: Proposes a dual-stream attacker with parallel encoders for spectral and self-supervised learning features, using three-stage training: Stage I establishes speaker-discriminative representations; Stage II leverages shared identity-transformation characteristics of voice conversion and anonymization to build cross-system robustness; Stage III provides lightweight adaptation to target anonymized data.
AI.result: Results on VoicePrivacy Attacker Challenge dataset show Stage II is primary driver of generalization, enabling strong attacking performance on unseen anonymization datasets. With Stage III, fine-tuning on only 10% of target anonymization dataset surpasses current state-of-the-art attackers in terms of Equal Error Rate (EER).
AI.conclusion: The proposed three-stage training strategy effectively improves privacy evaluation of voice anonymization systems, with Stage II providing crucial cross-system generalization and Stage III enabling efficient adaptation to specific anonymization methods.

title: Compensation of Input/Output Delays for Retarded Systems by Sequential Predictors: A Lyapunov-Halanay Method
summary: This paper presents a Lyapunov-Halanay method to study global asymptotic stabilization (GAS) of nonlinear retarded systems subject to large constant delays in input/output - a challenging problem due to their inherent destabilizing effects. Under the conditions of global Lipschitz continuity (GLC) and global exponential stabilizability (GES) of the retarded system without input delay, a state feedback controller is designed based on sequential predictors to make the closed-loop retarded system GAS. Moreover, if the retarded system with no output delay permits a global exponential observer, a dynamic output compensator is also constructed based on sequential predictors, achieving GAS of the corresponding closed-loop retarded system with input/output delays. The predictor based state and output feedback stabilization results are then extended to a broader class of nonlinear retarded systems with input/output delays, which may not be GES but satisfy global asymptotic stabilizability/observability and suitable ISS conditions. As an application, a pendulum system with delays in the state, input and output is used to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed state and output feedback control strategies based on sequential predictors.

AI.tldr: A Lyapunov-Halanay method is developed for global asymptotic stabilization of nonlinear retarded systems with large constant input/output delays using sequential predictor-based controllers.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the challenging problem of stabilizing nonlinear retarded systems subject to large constant delays in input/output, which have inherent destabilizing effects that complicate control design.
AI.method: Uses Lyapunov-Halanay method with sequential predictors to design state feedback controllers under GLC and GES conditions, and dynamic output compensators when global exponential observers exist. Extends to broader class of systems with ISS conditions.
AI.result: Achieves global asymptotic stabilization for nonlinear retarded systems with large delays using predictor-based state and output feedback controllers, with application to a pendulum system demonstrating effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The proposed sequential predictor-based approach successfully stabilizes nonlinear retarded systems with significant input/output delays, extending stabilization capabilities to systems with ISS properties beyond GES requirements.

title: Perpetual Dialogues: A Computational Analysis of Voice-Guitar Interaction in Carlos Paredes's Discography
comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, to be published in ICMC 2026
summary: Computational musicology enables systematic analysis of performative and structural traits in recorded music, yet existing approaches remain largely tailored to notated, score-based repertoires. This study advances a methodology for analyzing voice-guitar interaction in Carlos Paredes's vocal collaborations - an oral-tradition context where compositional and performative layers co-emerge. Using source-separated stems, physics-informed harmonic modelling, and beat-level audio descriptors, we examine melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic relationships across eight recordings with four singers. Our commonality-diversity framework, combining multi-scale correlation analysis with residual-based detection of structural deviations, reveals that expressive coordination is predominantly piece-specific rather than corpus-wide. Diversity events systematically align with formal boundaries and textural shifts, demonstrating that the proposed approach can identify musically salient reorganizations with minimal human annotation. The framework further offers a generalizable computational strategy for repertoires without notated blueprints, extending Music Performance Analysis into oral-tradition and improvisation-inflected practices.

AI.tldr: Computational analysis of voice-guitar interaction in Carlos Paredes's vocal collaborations reveals expressive coordination is piece-specific, with diversity events aligning with formal boundaries in oral-tradition music.
AI.motivation: Existing computational musicology approaches are tailored to notated, score-based repertoires, leaving a gap for analyzing oral-tradition contexts where compositional and performative layers co-emerge without written blueprints.
AI.method: Uses source-separated stems, physics-informed harmonic modeling, and beat-level audio descriptors to analyze melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic relationships across eight recordings with four singers. Implements a commonality-diversity framework combining multi-scale correlation analysis with residual-based detection of structural deviations.
AI.result: Expressive coordination is predominantly piece-specific rather than corpus-wide. Diversity events systematically align with formal boundaries and textural shifts, demonstrating the approach can identify musically salient reorganizations with minimal human annotation.
AI.conclusion: The framework offers a generalizable computational strategy for repertoires without notated blueprints, extending Music Performance Analysis into oral-tradition and improvisation-inflected practices.

title: On the strict-feedback form of hyperbolic distributed-parameter systems
summary: The paper is concerned with the strict-feedback form of hyperbolic distributed-parameter systems. Such a system structure is well known to be the basis for the recursive backstepping control design for nonlinear ODEs and is also reflected in the Volterra integral transformation used in the backstepping-based stabilization of parabolic PDEs. Although such integral transformations also proved very helpful in deriving state feedback controllers for hyperbolic PDEs, they are not necessarily related to a strict-feedback form. Therefore, the paper looks at structural properties of hyperbolic systems in the context of controllability. By combining and extending existing backstepping results, exactly controllable heterodirectional hyperbolic PDEs as well as PDE-ODE systems are mapped into strict-feedback form. While stabilization is not the objective in this paper, the obtained system structure is the basis for a recursive backstepping design and provides new insights into coupling structures of distributed-parameter systems that allow for a simple control design. In that sense, the paper aims to take backstepping for PDEs back to its ODE origin.

AI.tldr: The paper maps exactly controllable heterodirectional hyperbolic PDEs and PDE-ODE systems into strict-feedback form, providing a foundation for recursive backstepping control design and insights into distributed-parameter system coupling structures.
AI.motivation: While strict-feedback form is fundamental for recursive backstepping control of nonlinear ODEs and is reflected in Volterra transformations for parabolic PDEs, hyperbolic PDEs lack this structural connection despite using similar integral transformations. The paper aims to bridge this gap by establishing strict-feedback form for hyperbolic systems.
AI.method: The paper combines and extends existing backstepping results to map exactly controllable heterodirectional hyperbolic PDEs and PDE-ODE systems into strict-feedback form. This involves analyzing structural properties of hyperbolic systems in the context of controllability and establishing connections between integral transformations and strict-feedback structure.
AI.result: The paper successfully maps exactly controllable heterodirectional hyperbolic PDEs and PDE-ODE systems into strict-feedback form. This provides the structural foundation for recursive backstepping design and offers new insights into coupling structures of distributed-parameter systems that enable simpler control design.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a connection between hyperbolic PDEs and the strict-feedback form, bringing backstepping for PDEs back to its ODE origins. While stabilization is not the primary objective, the obtained system structure serves as the basis for recursive backstepping design and enhances understanding of distributed-parameter system coupling structures that facilitate straightforward control design.

title: From AI Weather Prediction to Infrastructure Resilience: A Correction-Downscaling Framework for Tropical Cyclone Impacts
summary: This paper addresses a missing capability in infrastructure resilience: turning fast, global AI weather forecasts into asset-scale, actionable risk. We introduce the AI-based Correction-Downscaling Framework (ACDF), which transforms coarse AI weather prediction (AIWP) into 500-m, unbiased wind fields and transmission tower/line failure probabilities for tropical cyclones. ACDF separates storm-scale bias correction from terrain-aware downscaling, preventing error propagation while restoring sub-kilometer variability that governs structural loading. Tested on 11 typhoons affecting Zhejiang, China under leave-one-storm-out evaluation, ACDF reduces station-scale wind-speed MAE by 38.8% versus Pangu-Weather, matches observation-assimilated mesoscale analyses, yet runs in 25 s per 12-h cycle on a single GPU. In the Typhoon Hagupit case, ACDF reproduced observed high-wind tails, isolated a coastal high-risk corridor, and flagged the line that failed, demonstrating actionable guidance at tower and line scales. ACDF provides an end-to-end pathway from AI global forecasts to operational, impact-based early warning for critical infrastructure.

AI.tldr: ACDF framework transforms coarse AI weather forecasts into high-resolution (500m) wind fields and transmission infrastructure failure probabilities for tropical cyclones, enabling actionable risk assessment for critical infrastructure.
AI.motivation: There's a gap in infrastructure resilience: AI weather forecasts are global and coarse, but actionable risk assessment requires asset-scale, high-resolution predictions. Current methods lack the ability to translate fast AI weather predictions into specific infrastructure failure probabilities.
AI.method: ACDF (AI-based Correction-Downscaling Framework) separates storm-scale bias correction from terrain-aware downscaling. It transforms coarse AI weather predictions into 500-meter resolution, unbiased wind fields and calculates transmission tower/line failure probabilities for tropical cyclones.
AI.result: Tested on 11 typhoons in Zhejiang, China with leave-one-storm-out evaluation: reduced station-scale wind-speed MAE by 38.8% vs Pangu-Weather, matched observation-assimilated mesoscale analyses, ran in 25 seconds per 12-hour cycle on single GPU. In Typhoon Hagupit case, reproduced observed high-wind tails, identified coastal high-risk corridor, and correctly flagged the line that actually failed.
AI.conclusion: ACDF provides an end-to-end pathway from AI global forecasts to operational, impact-based early warning for critical infrastructure, enabling actionable guidance at tower and line scales for tropical cyclone risk assessment.

title: EMT and RMS Modeling of Thyristor Rectifiers for Stability Analysis of Converter-Based Systems
summary: Thyristor rectifiers are a well-established and cost-effective solution for controlled high-power rectification, commonly used for hydrogen electrolysis and HVDC transmission. However, small-signal modeling and analysis of thyristor rectifiers remain challenging due to their line-commutated operation and nonlinear switching dynamics. This paper first revisits conventional RMS-based modeling of thyristor rectifiers and subsequently proposes a novel nonlinear state-space EMT model in the dq domain that can be linearized for small-signal analysis. The proposed model accurately captures all the relevant dynamic phenomena, including PLL dynamics, the commutation process, and switching delays. It is derived in polar coordinates, offering novel insights into the impact of the PLL and commutation angle on the thyristor rectifier dynamics. We verify the RMS and EMT models against a detailed switching model and demonstrate their applicability through small-signal stability analysis of a modified IEEE 39-bus test system that incorporates thyristor rectifier-interfaced hydrogen electrolyzers, synchronous generators, and grid-forming converters.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a novel nonlinear state-space EMT model for thyristor rectifiers in dq domain that can be linearized for small-signal analysis, addressing challenges in modeling line-commutated rectifiers for applications like hydrogen electrolysis and HVDC.
AI.motivation: Thyristor rectifiers are cost-effective for high-power applications like hydrogen electrolysis and HVDC, but their small-signal modeling is challenging due to line-commutated operation and nonlinear switching dynamics, requiring better analytical tools for stability analysis.
AI.method: The paper first revisits conventional RMS-based modeling, then proposes a novel nonlinear state-space EMT model in dq domain that can be linearized for small-signal analysis. The model is derived in polar coordinates and captures PLL dynamics, commutation process, and switching delays.
AI.result: The proposed model accurately captures all relevant dynamic phenomena and is verified against detailed switching models. Its applicability is demonstrated through small-signal stability analysis of a modified IEEE 39-bus test system with thyristor rectifier-interfaced hydrogen electrolyzers, synchronous generators, and grid-forming converters.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully develops a comprehensive modeling framework for thyristor rectifiers that enables accurate small-signal stability analysis, providing novel insights into PLL and commutation angle impacts on rectifier dynamics for modern power system applications.

title: Unifying Decision Making and Trajectory Planning in Automated Driving through Time-Varying Potential Fields
summary: This paper proposes a unified decision making and local trajectory planning framework based on Time-Varying Artificial Potential Fields (TVAPFs). The TVAPF explicitly models the predicted motion via bounded uncertainty of dynamic obstacles over the planning horizon, using information from perception and V2X sources when available. TVAPFs are embedded into a finite horizon optimal control problem that jointly selects the driving maneuver and computes a feasible, collision free trajectory. The effectiveness and real-time suitability of the approach are demonstrated through a simulation test in a multi-actor scenario with real road topology, highlighting the advantages of the unified TVAPF-based formulation.

AI.tldr: A unified decision-making and trajectory planning framework using Time-Varying Artificial Potential Fields (TVAPFs) that models dynamic obstacle motion with uncertainty and integrates perception/V2X data for real-time autonomous driving.
AI.motivation: To address the need for integrated decision-making and trajectory planning in autonomous driving that can handle dynamic obstacles with motion uncertainty, leveraging available perception and V2X information for safe navigation in complex multi-actor scenarios.
AI.method: Time-Varying Artificial Potential Fields (TVAPFs) that explicitly model predicted motion of dynamic obstacles with bounded uncertainty over planning horizon; embedded into finite horizon optimal control problem that jointly selects driving maneuvers and computes feasible, collision-free trajectories.
AI.result: Demonstrated effectiveness and real-time suitability through simulation tests in multi-actor scenarios with real road topology, showing advantages of the unified TVAPF-based formulation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed TVAPF framework successfully unifies decision-making and local trajectory planning, handling dynamic obstacles with motion uncertainty while maintaining real-time performance suitable for autonomous driving applications.
